# [CS022] Insecure Randomness for Security Value (crypto-weak-rand)

math/rand generates a token, key, password or nonce.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-338](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/338.html) |
| **OWASP** | A04:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

math/rand and math/rand/v2 generators are not cryptographically secure; their output can be predicted from earlier values. Use crypto/rand, for example rand.Text for tokens (Go 1.24).

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
token := fmt.Sprintf("%x", mathrand.Int63())
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
token := rand.Text() // crypto/rand, Go 1.24
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [crypto-weak-rand]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    crypto-weak-rand: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore crypto-weak-rand -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** crypto-weak-rand
```
